hypothesis: Exploit MLP hidden-neuron permutation symmetry to improve the existing adaptive weight-container coder without retraining or selecting on corpus scores.

recipes.mlp-scale: Stable ascending absolute bfloat16 up-projection row scale
recipes.mlp-zero-count: Stable ascending count of zero values in each up-projection row
recipes.mlp-row-mean: Stable ascending signed integer sum of each up-projection row (all rows have width 192)

transformation: For each of 16 MLP layers, reorder up.weight.q rows, up.weight.scale entries, and down.weight.q columns with the same permutation. All other tensors and container coding remain unchanged.
acceptance: The unchanged tensor set rewrites to the byte-identical upstream container
Inverse permutations restore all original tensor bytes
Each generated container reads back to its exact intended tensor set
Retain all three outcomes, including losses
promotion: Any size winner needs bit-exact tests of the actual up/down kernels including sparse/dense paths
Then compare identical input coder traces and archives on Mac and native Linux
Rebuild bound submission binaries and measure complete package size before claiming prize savings
scope: Container-only screening. Doubling a container delta is a gross estimate, not a prize score. Kernel equivalence and full-corpus predictions are initially unverified.
